# Acute Surgery

This folder contains the specific clinical quality indicators and related medical concepts used by the Akut Kirurgi Databasen (AKDB) to monitor and improve acute high-risk abdominal surgery in Denmark. It details the definitions, performance standards, and regional variations for metrics tracking everything from early antibiotic administration and preoperative optimization to postoperative mobilization, nutrition, epidural use, and 30- to 90-day mortality. The pages extensively document significant definitional shifts between the 2023 and 2024 reporting periods, reflecting the database's ongoing methodological adjustments, evolving clinical priorities, and the practical challenges of data registration in Danish hospitals.

## Pages

- [[akut-abdomen|akut abdomen]] — The primary clinical condition and patient population that defines the scope of the database's quality measurements.
- [[antibiotikabehandling]] — The essential first-line medical intervention for suspected acute abdominal infections, monitored for timely administration to reduce sepsis mortality.
- [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] — Measures the proportion of patients receiving antibiotics within three hours of hospital arrival, revealing significant logistical hurdles and regional disparities.
- [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] — Transitioned from tracking time-to-CT-scan to measuring preoperative physiological optimization or direct transfer to surgery within four hours.
- [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] — Shifted focus from preoperative optimization to tracking the proportion of acute patients operated on within six hours of arrival.
- [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] — Evolved from measuring surgical speed to monitoring the postoperative intermediate care admission of high-risk elderly or severely ill patients.
- [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] — Redefined from intermediate care tracking to measuring early postoperative mobilization within 24 hours, facing significant electronic health record registration challenges.
- [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] — Shifted from early mobilization to assessing postoperative nutritional care and the resumption of oral intake within 48 hours.
- [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] — Represents two different metrics across reporting years: early postoperative nutritional assessment and the administration of epidural anesthesia.
- [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]] — Transitioned from a process metric for epidural anesthesia use to an outcome indicator measuring 30-day postoperative mortality.
- [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] — Tracks postoperative survival, expanding its scope from 30-day to 90-day mortality to capture delayed deaths and evaluate Charlson Score risk adjustments.
- [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] — Measures 90-day mortality for acute surgery patients, highlighting institutional outliers and data quality issues regarding underlying comorbidities.
